captions.detailed: This 3D model consists of two separate components: a hollow main housing body and a flat sliding lid. The main housing is a rectangular box with rounded corners on one side, featuring a large internal cavity, a wide rectangular cable egress slot, and small rectangular zip-tie attachment slits on its rear wall. The lid is a flat plate with rounded corners on its corresponding side, equipped with thin, vertical guide tabs along its edges that slide into the main housing to secure it in place.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric docking connector housing in OpenSCAD consisting of a hollow main body and a matching sliding lid. The main body should feature adjustable width, length, height, a cable opening, and zip-tie slots, while the lid should include matching guide tabs for a secure slide-in fit.
captions.factory: The code defines the assembly by combining a main body and a lid. The main body is created using a 'difference' operation between a 'basicshape' (a union of a rounded box and a standard cube) and an 'innercavity' (a slightly smaller scaled version of the same shape), while also subtracting rectangular 'cableopening' and 'ziptieopenings' modules. The sliding lid is built by unioning a thin flat plate (using roundedBox and cube) with several small rectangular guide tabs ('cube') positioned to slide into the main body, accompanied by 'lowergripper' tabs on the body for alignment.
